summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and peripheral artery disease was admitted for fevers, diarrhea, and a worsening rash. He had a history of calciphylaxis and a chronic left leg ulcer. During admission, the leg wound was found to have necrotizing fasciitis, requiring surgical debridement and a wound VAC. He was treated with piperacillin-tazobactam for polymicrobial infection. A possible aortic valve vegetation raised concern for endocarditis, but TEE ruled it out. He underwent left femoral artery stenting for inflow stenosis. Hypertension was difficult to control and required multiple medication changes, including adding minoxidil and a clonidine patch. His hand pain was attributed to microvascular disease. He improved clinically and was discharged home on IV antibiotics, wound VAC care, and revised medications, with follow-up planned for wound closure and transplant management.
